transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery and recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. First of all, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question! You should avoid any exercise for the first week after your surgery. After that week, you can go back to light exercise like gardening. So you should be fine to start gentle gardening from about a week onwards.

Just remember to avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous work for about a month after your surgery.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information. Yes, I do have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it after surgery, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, I don't have the specific details about your particular eye gel in my information. If you're unsure whether it's safe to start using it again, I'd recommend checking with your care team or GP to be certain.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying that! Yes, I have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let us know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful. I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week ago, so it sounds like some blurriness is still normal at this point. Thank you for the information. I don't have any more questions right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's good to hear! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
